text: exact: the source's LC name authority (its URI, or its heading as LC prints it) or ORCID is on a key.

Candidates: keys with the same family name whose given names agree (name_level): 'full' = first given names written out and identical; 'variant' = a short form or transliteration (Ben/Benjamin, also Norma/Norman); 'initial' = an initial on either side. Jim and James do not agree at all.

A candidate is set aside as a different person (state none, 'only-proven-namesakes') when it holds an LC authority other than the source's, or its life years differ from the LC dates of the source by more than a year, or its PhD/works fall before the source person's age 15/20 or its articles after the source person's death.

Date test: the work's year inside the key's career window (birth+20, else PhD-10; to death+2, no upper bound for books); a key with neither, inside its own dated works widened SPAN_BEFORE/SPAN_AFTER years (SPAN_MIN works at least); a key with no dated work fails. A pooled key, a key whose birth and PhD contradict, or a key holding a different ORCID never passes (kept as possible).

linked 'unique-rare': exactly one candidate, it passes the date test, the names agree 'full', and the name is rare outside the graph: no other LC name authority bears the family + first given name (RARE_LC others) and at most RARE_OA OpenAlex History author ids do.

linked 'unique-second-fact': exactly one candidate, it passes the date test, and an independent fact ties it to the work: the printed institution's ROR is one of the key's dated affiliations (system names excluded), a co-author exact-linked on the same work is a known co-author of the key, the OpenAlex author id is tied to the key through another work the graph credits to it, or the work cites the key's own works. Needed when the name is common, 'variant' or 'initial'.
linked 'several-one-survives': several candidates, exactly one passes the date and contradiction tests, and it has such a fact.
Co-citation (theses citing both the work and the key's works) is recorded as support only: topic never links.
Everything else with a candidate is possible (candidates listed); no name-compatible key is none.

Round 2 (2026-11-10): span margin after 20 years, 10 for a key dated by a single work; 'unique-rare-fullname': the first two given names printed alike on both sides (or an initial against a name, when LC holds no other authority with that first name + initial), no other LC authority and at most 10 OpenAlex ids with them; 'unique-rare-variant': a spelling variant of 5+ letters (Sebastián/Sebastiaan), rare counting both spellings; dating for keys without window or span: the years of their works as the dissertation corpus cites them, their supervision and dated affiliations (-35/+25), or the first year a thesis cites them (-50, lower bound only); a key's supervision/affiliations/cited works before the source person was 20 prove two people; second fact added: a thesis the key supervised cites the work (not for variant/initial names, nor self-citation); a different ORCID on the key yields to a second fact; an OpenAlex ORCID whose owner agrees only by initial or variant while another key carries the printed name in full does not credit (L. H. / Lyndal Roper). Tried and not admitted: same journal (a proven namesake link), cited by the key's own thesis (a proven namesake link), printed institution name without ROR (no gold yield).
